sections.heading: 1. Pure Substances and Mixtures
points: A **pure substance** = made of only one kind of particle (**elements** and **compounds**).
A **mixture** = two or more substances mixed physically, in **any ratio**, keeping their own properties.

sub: **Heterogeneous** — not uniform (e.g. sand + water, oil + water).

sections.heading: 2. Solutions, Suspensions and Colloids
points: **Solution** — a **homogeneous** mixture (solute + solvent); particles very small; **does not scatter light**; e.g. salt water.
**Suspension** — a **heterogeneous** mixture with large particles that **settle down** and **scatter light** (e.g. muddy water, chalk in water).
**Colloid** — particles intermediate in size; appears uniform but **scatters light (Tyndall effect)**; does not settle (e.g. milk, fog, ink).

sections.heading: 3. Concentration of a Solution
points: **Concentration** = amount of solute in a given amount of solution/solvent.
**Dilute vs concentrated**; a **saturated** solution can dissolve no more solute at that temperature.
Solubility of most solids **increases with temperature**.

sections.heading: 4. Separating Mixtures
points: **Evaporation** (recover soluble solid, e.g. salt), **filtration** (insoluble solid), **centrifugation** (fine suspended particles), **separating funnel** (immiscible liquids).
**Sublimation** (e.g. camphor, ammonium chloride), **chromatography** (dyes/pigments), **distillation** (miscible liquids by boiling point), **fractional distillation** (e.g. air/petroleum).
**Crystallisation** = obtaining pure crystals from a solution (better than simple evaporation).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Pure substances = elements + compounds; mixtures = physically mixed (homogeneous/heterogeneous).
Solution = homogeneous, no light scattering; suspension = settles, scatters light; colloid = Tyndall effect, doesn't settle.
Tyndall effect = scattering of light by colloid particles (e.g. milk, fog).
Separation: evaporation, filtration, centrifugation, separating funnel, sublimation, chromatography, distillation.
Crystallisation gives pure crystals.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **colloid** shows the **Tyndall effect** (scatters light) but its particles **do not settle**; a **suspension** settles.
A **solution** is **homogeneous** and does **not** scatter light.
**Sublimation** separates substances like **camphor/ammonium chloride** (solid → gas directly).
**Fractional distillation** separates miscible liquids with close boiling points (e.g. petroleum, air).
